Interlocutory Application, This Day, The Court Delivered
The Following:
 -4-
 Nc: 2024:Khc-D:11403
 Mfa No. 100275 of 2020
 C/W Mfa.Crob No. 100043 of 2024
 Oral Judgment

MFA No.100275/2020 is filed by the insurance company challenging the quantum of compensation,
whereas MFA Crob No.100043/2024 is filed by the claimants seeking higher compensation being aggrieved by judgment and award dated 21.10.2019 passed in MVC No.1171/2018 on the file of learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT-XIII, Hagaribommanahalli1.
2.

Learned counsel Sri. G.N. Raichur for the appellant/insurer would submit that the Tribunal committed a grave error in treating all the three claimants as dependents of the deceased and awarded compensation.

He further submits that the claimants No.1 and 2 are major son and daughter of the deceased and they are not depending on the income of the deceased, hence, they cannot be termed as dependents, but they are entitled to compensation towards loss of estate only and not compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

He further submits that driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license with 'Transport' endorsement and therefore, saddling of liability on the insurer is contrary to law and therefore, seeks to saddle liability on the 'Tribunal', for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:11403 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100043 of 2024 owner of the offending vehicle.
He also submits that the Tribunal committed further error in awarding rate of interest at 8% per annum, which is on the higher side.
Thus, he seeks to allow the appeal filed by the insurer.

3. Per contra, learned counsel Sri. Gurukumar V.A. for the cross-objectors/claimants, at the outset,
submits that the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Birender & Others2 has held that even major children are also entitled to claim compensation.

National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Birender & Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month and award of compensation by the Tribunal under each heads is on the lower side.
Hence, he seeks to allow the cross-objection by dismissing the appeal of the insurer.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record including original records of the Tribunal.
5. It is not in dispute that in a road accident on 18.1.2018, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same.

It is also not in dispute that the (2020) 11 SCC 356 NC:
2024:KHC-D:11403 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100043 of 2024 accident has occurred due to negligence of driver of Tempo bearing registration No.KA-37-2828, which is insured with respondent/insurer.
6. Insofar as contention of the insurer that the driver of the Tempo was not having an endorsement on the DL to drive Transport goods vehicle.

The said contention is taken note of only for the purpose Devaramane Gurubasavaraja S/O Late ... vs H Lokeshgoudru S/O Somanagoudru on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160774898/
4 of rejection, since the said issue is squarely covered by a decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited3.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of enunciation of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Mukund Dewangan supra, the insurer of the offending Tempo is liable to pay compensation.

7. Insofar as contention with regard to dependents of the deceased is concerned, the claimant No.1 is the son of the deceased, aged about 27 years and he is a coolie as shown in the cause title; claimant No.2 is the daughter of the deceased aged about 28 years and claimant No.3 is the mother of deceased.

Taking note of pleadings and evidence available on record, I am of the considered view that the claimants No.1 and 2 may are major at the time of death of their father, however, AIR 2017 SC 3668 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11403 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100043 of 2024 there is no evidence on record to say that they are not fully dependents of the deceased.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Birender's case supra at paragraph-15 has held as under:
"15.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependant on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.........."

8. In view of enunciation of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgment referred supra, I am of the considered view that the claimant No.1 and 2 are considered as 'dependents' of the deceased for the purpose of determining compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
Accordingly, the said contention of insurer is rejected.
9. Insofar as entitlement of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month.
Admittedly, the claimants have not produced any cogent and acceptable evidence on record to assess notional income of the deceased.

This Court would re-assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.11,750/- per month placing reliance on notional income NC: 2024:KHC-D:11403 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100043 of 2024 chart prepared by KSLSA.
25% of the said income is added towards loss of future prospects and deduction would be 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
Thus, loss of dependency is re

- calculated as under:
Rs.11,750 + 25% x 12 x 13 x 2/3 = Rs.15,27,500/-
10.

The appellants are children and mother of the deceased and they are entitled to Rs.40,000/-
each towards loss of consortium, besides Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to modified compensation as under:
 Loss of dependency Rs.15,27,500/-
 Loss of consortium Rs. 1,20,000/-

Gurubasavaraja

5  Loss of estate & funeral expenses Rs. 30,000/-
 ------------------
 Total Rs.16,77,500/-

11.
The Tribunal committed an error in awarding higher rate of interest i.e., 8% per annum on the compensation amount.
Taking note of present day's bank rate of interest, this Court is inclined to reduce the rate of interest from 8% per annum to 6% per annum on the entire compensation.

12. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11403 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100043 of 2024 ORDER a) The appeal as well as cross-objection are allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the cross- objectors/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.16,77,500/- as against Rs.12,60,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The entire compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
d) The appellant/insurer shall deposit the entire compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) The apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per award of Tribunal.
f) The amount in deposit, if any, be transmitted to the Tribunal along with TCR forthwith.
g) Draw modified award accordingly.
